subject: DPA negotiation: Limited model training use & transfer controls (Medalytics)

Cc: Tom Blake <tom.blake@medalytics.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Initial redlines - DPA (Medalytics)

Hi Olga,

Thanks for sending over the standard DPA. Our legal team reviewed and attached redlines; the primary outstanding item is a carve-out to prohibit use of Customer Data to train machine learning models or otherwise improve models (including derivatives) unless expressly agreed in writing.

High-level asks:
- Add explicit prohibition: “Provider shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve models used in Provider’s services.”
- Define "Customer Data" to include any recorded input, document, or metadata related to Medalytics’ customers.
- Require that any de-identification/aggregation be validated by an independent process before use.
- No cross-border transfers of Customer Data for model development without prior written consent.

Attached: Medalytics_DPA_redlines_20261129.pdf (redlined DPA).

Please confirm receipt and next steps. We’d like to close the DPA this week if possible.

Best,
Amanda Cho
Sr. Counsel, Legal Ops
Medalytics

From: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
To: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-12-01T08:55:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: proposed compromise language for Medalytics DPA

Team — drafting a compromise that balances Medalytics’ concern with our operational needs. Proposed clause to present:

"Provider shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise create or improve models used for general product development or third-party services. Provider may, however, use: (i) aggregated, non-attributed metrics and telemetry that cannot be re-associated with a specific customer; and (ii) strictly de-identified data that has undergone a documented de-identification process, for purposes of service quality, anomaly detection, and system performance improvements. Any use falling within (ii) shall be subject to Provider’s internal de-identification policies and subject to audit upon reasonable notice. Provider shall not transfer Customer Data outside the customer’s specified geographic region for the purposes described in this paragraph without Customer's prior written consent."

Notes:
- Add a 90-day time-box for post-production telemetry retention if customer requests (we can support).
- Recommend we offer an exception for urgent security/abuse investigations (standard carve-out).
- We should propose a simple attestation: Provider will provide a summary of de-identification methods on request and, if necessary, independent attestation at cost to Customer.

Priyom — can you confirm if Medalytics will accept a 90-day telemetry retention window for service quality?

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Amanda Cho <amanda.cho@medalytics.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Tom Blake <tom.blake@medalytics.com>, Sarah Lin <sarah@privacycounsel.co>
Date: 2026-12-01T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DPA negotiation: Proposed clause review

Olga / Neha — thanks for the thoughtful compromise language. Medalytics can accept limited telemetry/aggregated metrics provided:

- Telemetry is strictly non-attributable (no customer IDs, org names, or persistent identifiers);
- Any retention period is explicitly time-boxed and agreed in the DPA; we propose 90 days maximum;
- Any independent attestation of de-identification should be performed by a mutually-agreed third party and costs borne by Provider unless a material non-compliance is found.

We’re not comfortable with a general security exception to allow training; security/abuse investigations are fine but must be narrowly scoped and documented.

Attached: Medalytics_DPA_counter_20261201.pdf (counter redline with minor edits). Can we get a DocuSign ready version for signatures once final text is confirmed?

Best,
Amanda Cho
Sr. Counsel, Legal Ops
Medalytics

Subject: Re: DPA negotiation: Final clause suggestion & execution steps

Hi all — external counsel for Medalytics here. Per discussions, we propose the following redline-ready paragraph for insertion into Section 4 (Permitted Uses):

"4.3 Model Use Limitation. Provider shall not use, access, or process Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve machine learning models that are used outside the scope of Customer’s contracted services. Provider may process aggregated, non-attributable telemetry or de-identified data for the limited purposes of service quality, performance optimization, and anomaly detection, provided that: (a) such telemetry cannot be reasonably re-identified with Customer or Customer’s end users; (b) retention is limited to 90 days by default unless mutually agreed otherwise; and (c) any de-identification attestation is provided by an independent third party agreed by the parties (costs borne by Provider except where non-compliance is found). Any use beyond the foregoing requires Customer’s prior written consent."

If that works, Amanda can confirm and I can circulate an execution-ready PDF. We prefer DocuSign for signatures; DocuSign envelope prepped and ready — see link below.
